room_name: Le service des visas · The visa and passport office
hook: "ee-dahn-tee-fee-kah-SYOHN": a clerk at a side desk holds up a man's ID card and checks the photo on it: IDENTIFICATION: IDENTIFICATION
note: Cognate of English identification. L'identification is identifying someone or something (l'identification d'un suspect; une pièce d'identification). It also means identifying with someone, as with a character in a film (l'identification au héros). The verb is identifier; s'identifier à means to identify with.

room_name: Le service des visas · The visa and passport office
hook: "soo-mee-SYOHN": a weary traveler kneels and waves a white handkerchief at a stern clerk with folded arms: he gives in, total SUBMISSION: SUBMISSION
note: Cognate of English submission. La soumission is submission, giving in to someone's power (la soumission à l'autorité); its opposite is la révolte or la résistance. In business it is also a tender or bid (une soumission pour un marché public). To submit a form is usually déposer or remettre, not soumettre.

room_name: Le service des visas · The visa and passport office
hook: "bree-tah-NEEK": a young woman sits on a suitcase covered with a big Union Jack sticker: BRITISH: BRITISH
note: Cognate of English British. Britannique means British (un passeport britannique; les îles Britanniques = the British Isles). Un Britannique, une Britannique is a British person, with a capital letter. English alone is anglais, and Breton (from Brittany, in France) is breton: a different place.

room_name: Le service des visas · The visa and passport office
hook: "tee-tew-LEHR": a proud man wears a gold championship TITLE belt and holds up his own passport: he is its TITLE-HOLDER: TITLE-holder
note: Cognate of English titular. Titulaire means holding a post or document in your own name: le titulaire du passeport (the passport holder), un professeur titulaire (a tenured teacher), un joueur titulaire (a first-team player, not a substitute). Its opposite is remplaçant or suppléant (a substitute) and, for teachers, contractuel.

room_name: Le service des visas · The visa and passport office
hook: "dee-ploh-mah-TEEK": two diplomats in dark suits shake hands at the counter: DIPLOMATIC talks: DIPLOMATIC
note: Cognate of English diplomatic. Diplomatique means diplomatic, about relations between countries (un passeport diplomatique, la valise diplomatique = the diplomatic bag) and, of a person, tactful (une réponse diplomatique). Its opposite in the second sense is maladroit or brutal (tactless).

room_name: Le service des visas · The visa and passport office
hook: "pehr-mah-NAHN": a stonemason chisels a blank stone tablet leaning on the wall: carved in stone, it is PERMANENT: PERMANENT, set in stone
note: Cognate of English permanent. Permanent means permanent, lasting (un titre de séjour permanent; un contrat permanent) or constant (un danger permanent). Its opposite is temporaire or provisoire. Une permanence is a duty office or open hours (la permanence du député); une permanente is a perm in hair.

room_name: Le service des visas · The visa and passport office
hook: "ohs-trah-LYAN": a young backpacker in a bush hat holds a wooden boomerang while he waits his turn: AUSTRALIAN: AUSTRALIAN
note: Cognate of English Australian. Australien means Australian (un passeport australien); fem. australienne. Un Australien, une Australienne is an Australian person, with a capital letter. Don't mix it up with autrichien (Austrian).

room_name: Le service des visas · The visa and passport office
hook: "oh-blee-gah-twah-ruh-MAHN": a security guard points sternly at yellow footprints painted on the floor where everyone OBLIGATORILY has to stand: OBLIGATORY
note: Cognate of English obligatorily. Obligatoirement means necessarily, compulsorily: Il faut obligatoirement un passeport (a passport is required). In speech it also means inevitably (Ça devait obligatoirement arriver = it was bound to happen). Its opposite is facultativement (optionally); pas obligatoirement means not necessarily.

room_name: Le service des visas · The visa and passport office
hook: "ahn-vwah-YAY": an ENVOY in a long dark coat with a blue sash hands a sealed letter with a red wax seal to an official: ENVOY
note: Cognate of English envoy. Un envoyé, une envoyée is an envoy, someone sent on a mission (un envoyé spécial = a special envoy, also a reporter sent abroad). It is the past participle of envoyer (to send). Un envoi is a parcel or a sending.

room_name: Le service des visas · The visa and passport office
hook: "kohn-sew-LAH": behind his own glass window, with a small foreign flag on his desk, a consul runs the CONSULATE counter: CONSULATE
note: Cognate of English consulate. Un consulat is a consulate, the office of a consul in a foreign city (le consulat de France à New York). Un consul runs it; une ambassade (embassy) is in the capital. Historically, le Consulat was France's government of 1799-1804, under Napoleon.

room_name: Le service des visas · The visa and passport office
hook: "vee-ZAH": at the counter a woman in a red coat holds up a big colorful stamped VISA page: VISA
note: Cognate of English visa. Un visa is a visa (un visa de tourisme; une demande de visa). It also means an official stamp of approval (le visa de censure for a film). The bank card brand is Visa too. Its opposite is un refus de visa (a visa refusal).

room_name: Le service des visas · The visa and passport office
hook: "for-mew-LEHR": an old man kneels on the floor filling in a FORM so long that it coils across the floor in big loops: FORM-ULAIRE
note: Un formulaire is a form to fill in (remplir un formulaire; un formulaire en ligne = an online form). Don't confuse it with une forme (a shape) or une formule (a formula or a set menu). Un formulaire vierge is a blank form.

room_name: Le service des visas · The visa and passport office
hook: "LAY-say-PASS": a guard lifts the red-and-white barrier arm and LETS a young man PASS when he shows a small pass card: LET-PASS
note: Un laissez-passer is a pass or permit that lets you through (un laissez-passer de presse; an emergency travel document for someone who lost a passport). Its plural is unchanged (des laissez-passer). Laisser passer, as a verb, means to let through; ne pas laisser passer means to refuse to let through.

room_name: Le service des visas · The visa and passport office
Le cabinet du maire · The mayor's office
hook: "ray-pew-BLEEK": an aide polishes a white plaster bust of MARIANNE in her soft cap, the symbol of the French REPUBLIC: MARIANNE of the REPUBLIC
note: Cognate of English republic. Une république is a republic, a state with an elected head and no king (la République française; la Ve République since 1958). Its opposite is une monarchie. In speech, en pleine république means in a free country; Marianne is its symbol in every town hall.

room_name: Le cabinet du maire · The mayor's office
hook: "mew-nee-see-pah-lee-TAY": a councilwoman traces with her finger the red boundary line around the whole village on a big framed aerial map: the MUNICIPALITY: MUNICIPALITY
note: Cognate of English municipality. La municipalité is the municipality, a town as a local government, and also its elected council and mayor (la municipalité a décidé... = the town council decided). The adjective is municipal. Une commune is the basic French local unit.

room_name: Le cabinet du maire · The mayor's office
hook: "kohn-fee-dahn-SYEHL": a secretary presses a big red seal onto a folder and holds a finger to her lips: CONFIDENTIAL: CONFIDENTIAL
note: Cognate of English confidential. Confidentiel means confidential, secret (un document confidentiel; à titre confidentiel = in confidence). It can also mean little known, for a small audience (un film confidentiel = a niche film). Its opposite is public.

room_name: Le cabinet du maire · The mayor's office
hook: "ehk-splee-see-tuh-MAHN": an aide points step by step at a big clear picture diagram on an easel (a house, an arrow, a key) and spells it all out EXPLICITLY: EXPLICITLY
note: Cognate of English explicitly. Explicitement means explicitly, clearly and in so many words (Il l'a dit explicitement). Its opposite is implicitement (implicitly, without saying it). The adjective explicite also describes adult content (des paroles explicites).

room_name: Le cabinet du maire · The mayor's office
hook: "ehg-zay-kew-TEEF": the boss sits in a big high-backed leather EXECUTIVE chair at the carved desk and signs a document with a fountain pen: EXECUTIVE
note: Cognate of English executive. Exécutif means executive, carrying out decisions: le pouvoir exécutif (the executive power: president and government), as opposed to législatif (making laws) and judiciaire (courts). L'exécutif is also a noun for the government. A business executive is un cadre.

room_name: Le cabinet du maire · The mayor's office
hook: "dees-KREH": a hunched young aide creeps DISCREETLY behind the boss's chair with her coffee, careful not to make a sound: DISCREET
note: Cognate of English discreet. Discret means discreet, keeping quiet about things (Sois discret !), and also modest, unobtrusive (une couleur discrète, un maquillage discret). Fem. discrète. Its opposite is indiscret (nosy, tactless) or voyant (flashy). In math it means discrete.

room_name: Le cabinet du maire · The mayor's office
hook: "an-TEHRN": a young INTERN pushes a cart of INTERNAL mail from office to office inside the building: INTERNAL INTERN
note: Cognate of English internal. Interne means internal, inside (le courrier interne = internal mail; une hémorragie interne). Its opposite is externe. Un interne, une interne is a hospital resident doctor or a boarder at school, not an office intern (that is un stagiaire).

room_name: Le cabinet du maire · The mayor's office
hook: "mee-nees-tay-RYEHL": a visiting government minister in a dark suit with a tiny tricolor lapel pin hugs his fat red leather MINISTERIAL portfolio: MINISTERIAL
note: Cognate of English ministerial. Ministériel means ministerial, of a government minister (un remaniement ministériel = a cabinet reshuffle; un arrêté ministériel = a ministerial order). Un ministre is a minister; le ministère is the ministry. It is not about church ministers.

room_name: Le cabinet du maire · The mayor's office
hook: "kah-tay-goh-ree-kuh-MAHN": an old farmer folds his arms and turns his head away with a stern frown from a saleswoman offering a giant novelty pen: no, CATEGORICALLY no!: CATEGORICALLY no
note: Cognate of English categorically. Catégoriquement means categorically, flatly (refuser catégoriquement; nier catégoriquement = to flatly deny). It is used most with refusals and denials. A softer opposite is avec hésitation or à demi (halfheartedly).

room_name: Le cabinet du maire · The mayor's office
hook: "goo-vehr-NUHR": a portly bank GOVERNOR in a pinstripe suit sits on a footstool and proudly holds up a fresh uncut sheet of new banknotes (blank play notes in the picture): GOVERNOR
note: Cognate of English governor. Un gouverneur is a governor: of a central bank (le gouverneur de la Banque de France), a colony or a US state. It comes from Latin gubernator, a ship's steersman. A school or prison governor is un directeur.

room_name: Le cabinet du maire · The mayor's office
hook: "goo-vehr-nuh-MAHN": on the paneling hangs a big framed painting of the GOVERNMENT: ministers sitting around one long table with the president: GOVERNMENT
note: Cognate of English government. Le gouvernement is the government: the prime minister and ministers (le gouvernement a démissionné = the cabinet resigned). It also means the act of governing. In France it is distinct from l'État (the state) and from l'administration (civil servants).

room_name: Le cabinet du maire · The mayor's office
hook: "kohn-fee-DAHN": an old man whispers a secret into the ear of his best friend, his CONFIDANT, who listens with a hand cupped to his ear: CONFIDANT
note: Cognate of English confidant. Un confident, une confidente is a confidant, someone you tell your secrets to (Elle est ma confidente). False friend: confident (sure of yourself) is sûr de soi or confiant. Une confidence is a secret you share (faire une confidence).

room_name: Le cabinet du maire · The mayor's office
La salle de presse · The press room
hook: "day-klah-rah-SYOHN": a spokeswoman at the podium reads out an official DECLARATION from a sheet of paper: DECLARATION
note: Cognate of English declaration. Une déclaration is a statement or declaration (faire une déclaration à la presse; la Déclaration des droits de l'homme). It is also a form you file (la déclaration d'impôts = tax return) and a declaration of love (une déclaration d'amour). Its opposite is un démenti (a denial).

room_name: La salle de presse · The press room
hook: "may-dyah-TEEK": a forest of MEDIA microphones on stands and a big TV camera crowd toward the podium: MEDIA
note: Cognate of English media. Médiatique means about the media (la couverture médiatique = media coverage; un événement médiatique). Said of a person, it means media-savvy or much in the media (un ministre très médiatique). Its rough opposite is discret or méconnu (low-profile). Les médias are the media.

room_name: La salle de presse · The press room
hook: "tehk-nee-kuh-MAHN": a TECHNICIAN on her knees untangles a huge knot of cables behind the TV camera: TECHNICALLY
note: Cognate of English technically. Techniquement means technically: in technical terms (techniquement parfait) and also strictly speaking, in theory (Techniquement, c'est interdit, mais...). Its opposite in the second sense is en pratique (in practice).

room_name: La salle de presse · The press room
hook: "ah-noh-NEEM": a man in a trench coat, hat and dark glasses hides his face behind a blank newspaper in the back row: ANONYMOUS: ANONYMOUS
note: Cognate of English anonymous. Anonyme means anonymous, unnamed (une lettre anonyme; un don anonyme). It also means faceless, impersonal (un immeuble anonyme). Une société anonyme (SA) is a public limited company. Its opposite is signé or connu.

room_name: La salle de presse · The press room
hook: "pah-rah-dok-sah-luh-MAHN": a man SHUSHES the noisy room through a giant megaphone, PARADOXICALLY making the most noise of all: PARADOXICALLY
note: Cognate of English paradoxically. Paradoxalement means paradoxically, against what you would expect (Paradoxalement, il travaille mieux fatigué). It is often used to introduce a surprising fact. The adjective is paradoxal; un paradoxe is a paradox.

room_name: La salle de presse · The press room
hook: "ee-nay-DEE": a reporter whips a cloth off an easel to reveal a never-before-seen UN-EDITED photo, and the room gasps: UN-EDITED
note: Inédit means never seen or published before (des photos inédites; un texte inédit) and, by extension, new, unprecedented (une situation inédite). False friend: it does not mean unedited (that is non retouché or brut). Its opposite is déjà vu or connu.

room_name: La salle de presse · The press room
hook: "VRAY SAHM-blab-luh-MAHN": a reporter-detective with a magnifying glass follows muddy paw prints to a puppy with a muddy nose: it SEEMS TRUE, PROBABLY the puppy did it: PROBABLY, VRAI SEMBLE
note: Vraisemblablement means probably, very likely (Il viendra vraisemblablement demain). It comes from vrai (true) and semblable (seeming): seemingly true. Its opposite is invraisemblablement or peu probablement. The adjective vraisemblable means plausible, likely.

room_name: La salle de presse · The press room
hook: "pew-blee-see-TEHR": an ad man unrolls a big colorful ADVERTISING poster of a smiling toothpaste tube for the cameras: PUBLICITY POSTER
note: Cognate of English publicity, but it means advertising. Publicitaire means about advertising (une affiche publicitaire = an advertising poster; un spot publicitaire = a commercial). Un publicitaire, une publicitaire is an advertising executive. Not publicity in the sense of fame, which is la notoriété; la publicité (la pub) is advertising.

room_name: La salle de presse · The press room
hook: "ee-roh-nee-kuh-MAHN": a TV weatherman proudly holds up a sunny forecast picture while water IRONICALLY drips on his head from a leak in the ceiling: IRONICALLY
note: Cognate of English ironically. Ironiquement means ironically: with irony, saying the opposite of what you mean (répondre ironiquement), and by an irony of fate (Ironiquement, il pleuvait le jour de la fête du soleil). The adjective is ironique.

room_name: La salle de presse · The press room
hook: "FOSS-MAHN": a young reporter in joke nose-and-mustache glasses grins FALSELY innocent: FALSELY
note: Faussement means falsely, wrongly (accusé faussement) or with pretense (faussement modeste = falsely modest; d'un air faussement innocent). Its opposite is vraiment or sincèrement. The adjective is faux, fausse (false, fake).

room_name: La salle de presse · The press room
hook: "poh-zee-tee-vuh-MAHN": a cheerful woman in the front row gives two big thumbs up, reacting POSITIVELY: POSITIVELY
note: Cognate of English positively. Positivement means positively, in a good way (réagir positivement) or in a definite way (C'est positivement faux = it's flat-out wrong). Its opposite is négativement. The adjective positif also means a positive test result.

room_name: La salle de presse · The press room
hook: "for-MAH": a kneeling photographer compares two empty picture frames, a tall one and a wide one, choosing the photo FORMAT: FORMAT
note: Cognate of English format. Le format is a format or size (le format A4; un format de poche = pocket-size; le format paysage = landscape format). It is also a computer file format (au format PDF). Formater means to format a disk, and figuratively to mold someone's mind.

room_name: La salle de presse · The press room
La salle du dépouillement · The ballot-counting room
hook: "ew-nah-nee-mee-TAY": three councilors at a table all raise their right hands at exactly the same moment: UNANIMITY: UNANIMITY
note: Cognate of English unanimity. L'unanimité is unanimity, everyone agreeing (voter à l'unanimité = to vote unanimously; faire l'unanimité = to win everyone over). Its opposite is la division or le désaccord; à la majorité means by a majority, not by everyone.

room_name: La salle du dépouillement · The ballot-counting room
hook: "kah-tay-goh-REE": a clerk sorts envelopes into three wire baskets, each one a different CATEGORY: CATEGORY
note: Cognate of English category. Une catégorie is a category or class (une catégorie d'âge; un hôtel de première catégorie = a first-class hotel). Catégoriel means sectional, for one group (des revendications catégorielles). Catégorique (categorical, flat) is a different word: un refus catégorique.

room_name: La salle du dépouillement · The ballot-counting room
hook: "proh-kew-rah-SYOHN": a woman with her leg in a big plaster cast, stuck at home for her CURE, holds up the PROXY form she has just signed so a friend can act FOR (PRO) her and vote in her place: PRO-CURE-ACTION: PRO-CURE-ACTION
note: Une procuration is a proxy, a written authorization to act for someone (voter par procuration = to vote by proxy; donner procuration à quelqu'un). In banking it is a power of attorney over an account. The person who receives it is le mandataire. Its opposite is acting in person, en personne.

room_name: La salle du dépouillement · The ballot-counting room
hook: "pree-MEHR": a little girl sits on the floor and paints with only the three PRIMARY colors, red, yellow and blue: PRIMARY
note: Cognate of English primary. Primaire means primary, first in order (les couleurs primaires; une élection primaire; l'école primaire = elementary school, for ages 6 to 11). Said of a person or idea, it is negative: simplistic, crude (un raisonnement primaire). Its opposite is secondaire.

room_name: La salle du dépouillement · The ballot-counting room
hook: "ay-lehk-toh-RAHL": two volunteers tip the big clear ELECTORAL ballot box upside down and a heap of envelopes pours onto the table: ELECTORAL
note: Cognate of English electoral. Électoral means about elections (une campagne électorale; la liste électorale = the voter roll; un bureau électoral). Fem. électorale, plural électoraux. L'électorat is the electorate, and un électeur, une électrice is a voter.

room_name: La salle du dépouillement · The ballot-counting room
hook: "deuh-zyeh-muh-MAHN": a teller in a bow tie holds up TWO fingers, DEUX, as he reads out his second point: secondly: DEUX (two)
note: Deuxièmement means secondly, in the second place, when listing points (Premièrement…, deuxièmement…). It is built on deuxième (second) from deux (two). Its partners are premièrement (firstly) and troisièmement (thirdly); in speech people often say ensuite or en second lieu instead.

room_name: La salle du dépouillement · The ballot-counting room
hook: "poh-lee-tee-kuh-MAHN": two men in red and blue ties talk POLITICALLY, each wagging a finger to make his point: POLITICALLY
note: Cognate of English politically. Politiquement means politically, from the point of view of politics (politiquement engagé = politically active; politiquement correct). Its opposite is apolitiquement, rarely used; people say sans parti pris (without taking sides) instead.

room_name: La salle du dépouillement · The ballot-counting room
hook: "rehs-pehk-tee-vuh-MAHN": twin boys in a red shirt and a blue shirt hold a red balloon and a blue balloon, RESPECTIVELY: RESPECTIVELY
note: Cognate of English respectively. Respectivement means respectively, each in the order given (Ils ont respectivement 8 et 10 ans = They are 8 and 10, respectively). It has nothing to do with respect; for respectfully say respectueusement.

room_name: La salle du dépouillement · The ballot-counting room
hook: "ay-kee-vah-LAHN": a volunteer sets two piles of envelopes on an old balance and the pans hang perfectly level: each pile is the EQUIVALENT of the other: EQUIVALENT
note: Cognate of English equivalent. Un équivalent is an equivalent, something of equal value or meaning (Il n'y a pas d'équivalent en anglais). It is also an adjective: équivalent à (equal to). Its opposite is une différence or un écart. The verb is équivaloir à, to amount to.

room_name: La salle du dépouillement · The ballot-counting room
hook: "see-twah-YAN": a proud boy holds his brand-new voter card high above his head: a CITIZEN voting for the first time: CITIZEN
note: Cognate of English citizen. Un citoyen, une citoyenne is a citizen, a member of the nation with rights and duties (un citoyen français; le devoir du citoyen). As an adjective it means civic-minded (un geste citoyen). La citoyenneté is citizenship. The opposite is un étranger, a foreigner.

room_name: La salle du dépouillement · The ballot-counting room
hook: "kohn-see-twah-YAN": two neighbors from the same village shake hands warmly: FELLOW CITIZENS: FELLOW CITIZEN
note: Cognate of English citizen, with con- meaning with: un concitoyen, une concitoyenne is a fellow citizen, someone from the same town or country (Mes chers concitoyens = My fellow citizens, a classic opening of a mayor's speech). Its opposite is un étranger, an outsider.

room_name: La salle du dépouillement · The ballot-counting room
La salle d'éducation civique · The civics classroom
hook: "deek-tah-TEWR": a little boy in a paper general's hat plays DICTATOR, arms crossed, barking orders at the whole class: a DICTATORSHIP: DICTATORSHIP
note: Cognate of English dictatorship (via dictator). Une dictature is a dictatorship, rule by one person or group with no free elections (vivre sous une dictature; la dictature militaire). Figuratively it means any tyranny (la dictature de la mode). Its opposite is la démocratie. The ruler is un dictateur.

room_name: La salle d'éducation civique · The civics classroom
change: added; vocab room R_politics_04 -> R_adj_relation_10; vocab example replaced (old one mentioned tobacco): 'La législation sur le bruit a changé.' / 'The legislation on noise has changed.'
hook: "lay-zhee-slah-SYOHN": a teacher piles yet another thick law book onto a wobbling tower of LEGISLATION: LEGISLATION
note: Cognate of English legislation. La législation is legislation, the body of laws on a subject (la législation du travail = labor law; la législation en vigueur = the laws in force). It is a collective noun: one single law is une loi. To legislate is légiférer.

room_name: La salle d'éducation civique · The civics classroom
hook: "SHAHRT": a girl unrolls a long parchment CHARTER with a red wax seal at the bottom: CHARTER
note: Cognate of English charter. Une charte is a charter, a founding text of rights or rules (la Charte des Nations unies; la charte de l'environnement; une charte de qualité = a code of practice). It is not a chart: a chart is un graphique or, at sea, une carte marine.

room_name: La salle d'éducation civique · The civics classroom
hook: "kohns-tee-tew-syoh-NEHL": a proud librarian holds up the big bound book of the CONSTITUTION with both hands: CONSTITUTIONAL
note: Cognate of English constitutional. Constitutionnel means constitutional, in line with the constitution (le Conseil constitutionnel; une loi constitutionnelle). Fem. constitutionnelle. Its opposite is anticonstitutionnel, unconstitutional. Said of a person's health it means constitutional too (une faiblesse constitutionnelle = an inborn weakness).

room_name: La salle d'éducation civique · The civics classroom
hook: "lay-zhee-slah-TEEF": a girl at a small lectern reads out a brand-new law to the class: LEGISLATIVE work: LEGISLATIVE
note: Cognate of English legislative. Législatif means legislative, about making laws (le pouvoir législatif = the legislature; les élections législatives = the parliamentary elections). Fem. législative. It goes with l'exécutif and le judiciaire, the three powers.

room_name: La salle d'éducation civique · The civics classroom
hook: "fay-day-RAHL": a finished jigsaw map lies on the floor, its separate colored regions joined into one FEDERAL country: FEDERAL
note: Cognate of English federal. Fédéral means federal, made of states united under a central government (l'État fédéral; la Suisse est un pays fédéral). Plural fédéraux. Its opposite is unitaire (a unitary state, like France) or centralisé. La fédération also means a sports federation.

room_name: La salle d'éducation civique · The civics classroom
hook: "pahr-luh-mahn-TEHR": a boy sets tiny figures in the red seats of a half-circle model PARLIAMENT: PARLIAMENTARY
note: Cognate of English parliamentary. Parlementaire means parliamentary (un régime parlementaire; le débat parlementaire). As a noun, un or une parlementaire is a member of parliament. Its root is parler, to speak. Do not confuse it with parlementer, to negotiate.

room_name: La salle d'éducation civique · The civics classroom
hook: "oh-toh-ree-TEHR": a strict gray-haired schoolmistress frowns and raises her ruler, about to rap the desk: AUTHORITARIAN: AUTHORITARIAN
note: Cognate of English authoritarian. Autoritaire means authoritarian or bossy (un régime autoritaire; un père autoritaire). It is a criticism, stronger than strict (sévère). Its opposite is libéral, permissif or souple. L'autorité is authority.

room_name: La salle d'éducation civique · The civics classroom
hook: "tay-oh-ree-kuh-MAHN": two children kneel by their real paper plane, crashed on the floor, right under the perfect chalk flight path on the board: it works THEORETICALLY: THEORETICALLY
note: Cognate of English theoretically. Théoriquement means theoretically or in principle, and it often hints that reality will differ (Théoriquement, il arrive à 8 h = He's supposed to arrive at 8). Its opposite is pratiquement or en pratique. Une théorie is a theory.

room_name: La salle d'éducation civique · The civics classroom
hook: "fohn-dah-mahn-tah-luh-MAHN": a girl points at the big bottom block that holds up her whole tall tower: FUNDAMENTALLY: FUNDAMENTALLY
note: Cognate of English fundamentally. Fondamentalement means fundamentally, at its very base (Ils sont fondamentalement différents). It comes from fondamental and le fondement, the foundation. Its opposite is superficiellement, superficially.

room_name: La salle d'éducation civique · The civics classroom
hook: "soh-syah-LEEZM": three workers in overalls share out the round loaves on one table equally: SOCIALISM: SOCIALISM
note: Cognate of English socialism. Le socialisme is socialism, the political idea of sharing wealth and owning key industries together (le socialisme utopique; le Parti socialiste). Its opposite is le capitalisme or le libéralisme. A follower is un or une socialiste.

room_name: La salle d'éducation civique · The civics classroom
hook: "goo-vehr-NAHN": a boy dressed as a king in a paper crown sits on a big carved chair, GOVERNING the class: a RULER: GOVERNING
note: Cognate of English governing (from gouverner, to govern). Un gouvernant is a ruler; it is mostly used in the plural, les gouvernants, those in power, as opposed to les gouvernés, the governed. Careful: une gouvernante is a housekeeper or governess, not a female ruler.

room_name: La salle d'éducation civique · The civics classroom
La salle des cérémonies · The ceremonial hall
hook: "ee-noh-gew-rah-SYOHN": the mayor in her blue-white-red sash snips the ribbon to open the new wing: the INAUGURATION: INAUGURATION
note: Cognate of English inauguration. Une inauguration is the official opening of a new building, road or exhibition (l'inauguration de la nouvelle école), usually with a ribbon cut by the mayor. It can also mean the start of a term of office, but that sense is rarer in French than in English. The verb is inaugurer.

room_name: La salle des cérémonies · The ceremonial hall
hook: "pray-zee-DAHNS": a woman rings the little brass bell from the tall gilded presiding chair: she holds the PRESIDENCY of the evening: PRESIDENCY
note: Cognate of English presidency. La présidence is the presidency, the office of president or its term (pendant sa présidence), and also the chairing of a meeting or body (assurer la présidence de la séance). La présidence also names the president's offices and staff (un communiqué de la présidence).

room_name: La salle des cérémonies · The ceremonial hall
hook: "ahk-seh-SYOHN": a little girl in a yellow dress climbs the last red-carpeted step up onto the stage: her ACCESSION to the top: ACCESSION
note: Cognate of English accession. L'accession is reaching a rank or a status (l'accession au trône; l'accession à l'indépendance). L'accession à la propriété means becoming a homeowner. It is a formal word; in everyday French people say l'accès or say arriver à.

room_name: La salle des cérémonies · The ceremonial hall
hook: "noh-mee-nah-SYOHN": a man reads a name off his card and a young woman jumps up, hand on her heart: her NOMINATION: NOMINATION
note: Cognate of English nomination. Une nomination is usually an appointment to a post (sa nomination au poste de directeur), not only a proposal. It is also a nomination for a prize (trois nominations aux César). The verb is nommer, to appoint or to name.

room_name: La salle des cérémonies · The ceremonial hall
hook: "ans-tee-tew-syoh-NEHL": on a stand stands the white model of the grand domed public building, the new INSTITUTION being opened: INSTITUTIONAL
note: Cognate of English institutional. Institutionnel means about institutions, the official bodies of the state (la réforme institutionnelle; une crise institutionnelle). Fem. institutionnelle. Une institution is an institution; une institutrice, un instituteur was the old word for a primary school teacher. Its opposite is informel.

room_name: La salle des cérémonies · The ceremonial hall
hook: "ray-pew-blee-KAN": a white bust of Marianne in her soft cap, the symbol of the French Republic, stands on a pedestal: REPUBLICAN: REPUBLICAN
note: Cognate of English republican. Républicain means of the Republic or loyal to it (les valeurs républicaines; la garde républicaine). In France it is not a party label as in the US; Les Républicains is the name of one right-wing party. Its opposite is monarchiste or royaliste.

room_name: La salle des cérémonies · The ceremonial hall
hook: "ray-zoh-lew-MAHN": a little drummer boy marches across the hall, jaw set and eyes straight ahead: RESOLUTELY: RESOLUTELY
note: Cognate of English resolutely. Résolument means resolutely, with firm determination (Elle est résolument contre ce projet). It often means decidedly or firmly in a style (un hôtel résolument moderne). It comes from résolu, determined. Its opposite is timidement or mollement.

room_name: La salle des cérémonies · The ceremonial hall
hook: "grahn-DYOHZ": an enormous five-tier white wedding-style cake stands right on the parquet floor in the middle of the hall: GRANDIOSE: GRANDIOSE
note: Cognate of English grandiose. Grandiose means magnificent or grand, and in French it is usually praise (un paysage grandiose; une cérémonie grandiose). In English grandiose often sounds pompous. Its opposite is modeste or mesquin.

room_name: La salle des cérémonies · The ceremonial hall
hook: "prehs-tee-ZHYEUH": a famous old actress in a white fur stole proudly holds up a glossy portrait of herself for her fans: a PRESTIGIOUS guest: PRESTIGIOUS
note: Cognate of English prestigious. Prestigieux means prestigious, admired and famous (une école prestigieuse; un prix prestigieux). Fem. prestigieuse. Le prestige is prestige. In older French it meant an illusion or a magic trick, a sense that is now lost.

room_name: La salle des cérémonies · The ceremonial hall
hook: "for-meh-luh-MAHN": a butler in tails and white gloves bows stiffly, very FORMALLY, holding out a silver tray: FORMALLY
note: Cognate of English formally. Formellement means formally, according to the rules (Il a été formellement invité), but very often it means strictly or explicitly (C'est formellement interdit = It is strictly forbidden; Je le nie formellement = I flatly deny it). Its opposite is vaguement or officieusement.

room_name: La salle des cérémonies · The ceremonial hall
hook: "vees-pray-zee-DAHN": a man sits in a second gilded chair, a little smaller than the presiding one: the VICE-PRESIDENT: VICE-PRESIDENT
note: Cognate of English vice-president. Un vice-président, une vice-présidente is a vice-president, the deputy of a president or chair (le vice-président du conseil départemental). France has no vice-president of the Republic: if the president leaves office, the president of the Senate stands in.

room_name: La salle des cérémonies · The ceremonial hall
hook: "say-nah-TUHR": a dignified white-haired SENATOR in a dark suit listens with his hands folded on his cane: SENATOR
note: Cognate of English senator. Un sénateur, une sénatrice is a senator, a member of the Sénat, France's upper house of parliament, elected indirectly by local councilors (le sénateur de la Corrèze). Its partner is le député, who sits in the Assemblée nationale.
